old_caption: The video begins with a close-up shot of a large cloud of dust billowing into the air. The dust is initially thick and opaque, obscuring the background. As the dust dissipates slowly and unevenly, a ground covered with dry leaves and twigs is revealed. A red and white object is visible through the clearing dust, lying on the ground. The scene is a natural, outdoor setting with a wooded environment featuring dense trees and underbrush.
original_wisa_caption: The video begins with a close-up shot of a large cloud of dust or smoke billowing into the air. The dust appears thick and opaque, obscuring much of the background. As the dust settles, the camera slowly pans to the right, revealing a forested area with dense trees and underbrush. The ground is covered with dry leaves and twigs, indicating a natural, outdoor setting. In the foreground, there is a red and white object lying on the ground, partially obscured by the dust. The camera continues to pan, showing more of the forest and the scattered debris on the ground. The scene suggests an explosion or some form of disturbance has occurred, leaving behind a cloud of dust and debris in a quiet, wooded environment.
caption: A close-range outdoor ground scene is almost entirely obscured by a bright, dense cloud of airborne dust and flying debris. Straw shards, dark flecks, and a pale green blade drift across the washed-out frame while the background remains indistinguishable. As the haze darkens and loses opacity, suspended particles continue to move through the field of view. The dark shrubbery and thin twigs behind a patch of dry straw gradually show through the murk. Visibility of the ground increases steadily, revealing scattered green leaves and a slender vertical twig standing on the right. A crumpled red-and-white bag-like object emerges left of center and holds its position as the dust thins. Only a few residual flecks continue to drift in the air as the cloud settles.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
